conclusion: No vendor-free Windows CPU temperature provider or exact672 ACPI/PDH CPU-zone mapping was recovered. Shared Synapse CPU package monitoring depends on its native CPUID monitoring stack; exact672 does not enable that shared monitoring feature.

sources.evidence: Exact672 deviceUI config identifies bladeSeries 9 and Intel CPU overclocking. Injection includes useMWManifest, deviceUI, runtimeCache, and device25LedMatrixBlade. No systemHelper or hasSystemMonitoringStatistics injection.

offsets.evidence: rzSystemMon starts only when hasSystemMonitoringStatistics is enabled.
Requires systemHelper.config clientDllName/serverDllName/externalDllName; resolves RzDLLService and native resources, registers callback, starts APP server if absent.
CPU Status enable selects Temperatures.Package cur/min/max. These are measured current/minimum/maximum values, not a throttle threshold.
Shared OLED presentation treats measured CPU temperature as Celsius and converts Fahrenheit with 9*x/5+32.
Series11 monitoring presentation includes fixed chart limit Temperature:100; this display scale is not a sensor reading.

sources.evidence: Exact672 native resource manifest pins BladeDLL and Intel overclocking resources.

exactManifestComponents.evidence: Export review: display/color management, GPU tuning, BIOS/EC version, serial number. No CPU temperature export or thermal-zone/PDH source recovered.
Exports asynchronous tuning-control operations and APP-server transport. No standalone CPU temperature getter.
Tuning-control API; XTU3SERVICE string at file offset 0x49fd0/RVA0x4b9d0. Missing/not-running Intel XTU OC Service errors at file offsets 0x4bd30 and 0x4bd98. Not a vendor-free provider.

sharedInstalledComponents.evidence: GetCPUTemperature export RVA0x6f420; GetCPUAndGPUTemperatureAndClock RVA0x70d90. Temperature CPU Package string at file offset0xac700/RVA0xad700.

GetCPUTemperature export RVA0x43c80; RzHWMonitorCPUZ::InitRzHardwareMonitor at file offset0x587b0/RVA0x59fb0; cpuidsdk64.dll at offset0x56c08/RVA0x58408. Explicit CPUID initialization errors. Visible PDH paths are LogicalDisk(C:) Disk Read/Write Bytes/sec at offsets0x5a600/0x5a690, not CPU temperature.

CPUID SDK with CPU Package sensors, MSR-related classes, and embedded CPUZ152/159 driver images. Processor Information PDH path at file offset0x213120 is Processor Utility. No Thermal Zone Information, MSAcpi thermal-temperature, or TZRZ string found in bounded static inspection.

interpretation: Native monitoring components are installed shared resources inspected only as architectural evidence; they are not pinned by the exact672 resource manifest and were not proven active for this model.
The presence of PDH APIs in CPUID SDK does not establish a CPU temperature PDH source; recovered named counters cover utilization and disk I/O.

No recovered evidence authorizes mapping every Windows thermal-zone counter to CPU package temperature. Generic enumeration may discover zones but their CPU meaning and exact-device availability remain unproven.
A missing CPU reading must remain unavailable; fixed display limits, Intel tuning controls, and throttling limits cannot substitute for measured temperature.
The recovered source does not justify adding runtime Synapse/XTU/CPUID dependencies, invoking drivers, or new firmware queries.
uncertainties: No physical CPU temperature observation was performed.
No exact672 ACPI namespace or PDH zone-to-CPU mapping was recovered.
Static inspection does not prove that no other vendor temperature provider exists; the requested manifest and shared monitor chain were bounded endpoints.
Installed common monitoring component versions are local evidence, not a complete exact672 deployment manifest.
validationBoundary: Read-only source inspection, HTTPS GET downloads, hashing, PE exports/strings, and static disassembly only. No vendor components executed, no DLLs loaded as code, no installations, no hardware calls, no new capture. Evidence collection made no repository edits.
